assumptions.what: The variance filter is the pooled within-group variance Sp^2 (the text's W_V is the variance of all samples S_Z^2)
assumptions.sensitivity: Under the null, S_Z^2 is independent of T and leaves the p-value density flat at 1; the published dotted curve falls to 0 at p = 0. With Sp^2 the three curves match the published ones within 0.001 (density units). S_Z^2 is a near-miss control.

assumptions.sensitivity: None.

assumptions.what: delta = 1 is the noncentrality of the t statistic
assumptions.sensitivity: With delta read as a group difference of 1 (noncentrality 1.58) the no-filter curve misses by up to 3.8; with the noncentrality the no-filter and fold-change curves match within 0.002. A near-miss control.

assumptions.what: The thresholds are set under the null and used under the alternative
assumptions.sensitivity: Thresholds set under the alternative itself move the fold-change curve by up to 0.52. A near-miss control.

assumptions.what: The variance filter is Sp^2, as for the null panel

The lost R scripts were rebuilt from the paper, the simulation and the leukemia analysis were run again, and every curve was laid over the authors' own vector figures.
page.items_caption: Every figure panel and claim of the paper and its Additional File 1. A figure panel agrees when 95% of the published ink lies within 2 px of ours and ours of it, at 300 dpi on the published panel's own axes, and no wrong or near-miss version scores as well.
page.claims_line: The main finding holds: the fold-change filter biases the FDR and raises power, and the signal and variance filters do not bias it. Three sentences overstate the paper's own figures, and Fig. 3's caption swaps two curves; the power gaps of Figs 5, S2, S5 and S6 are open.
came_back: Achieved FDR for four methods within 0.004 at every point but one.
pi0 for every filter within 0.004, once the caption's swapped labels are put back.
The null densities exactly, and two of the three alternative curves.
The test's box medians, from data without the noise term.
Simulation, filters, FDR-bias test and p-value densities as the R package filterfdr.
buried: The authors' R scripts: the paper's link and its zip are gone.
Seeds, the subsets drawn from the leukemia data, and the settings of bootFDR and permFDR (Figure S7).
Why the paper's power is a little higher than ours in Figs 5, S2, S5 and S6: tested causes ruled out.
page.matched_intro: How each part of the paper's method was rebuilt.
matched: 5000 features, 10 per group, pi0 0.8, bitriangular effects as in the first author's SSPA; noise SD 0.1 per feature.
Signal, fold change and variance, cut at their empirical quantiles.
BH, BY, multtest's two-stage aBH and qvalue, at 5% and at 21 levels.
Rows permuted one by one, BH-based KS per permutation, then a one-sided KS over 1000 permutations.
GSE13425, 44 TEL-AML1 against 44 hyperdiploid, limma, truth from all 88.
page.closing: Filtering, FDR and power came back from the paper's text and its vector figures; the scripts did not.
